title: Incident: detection, communication and blameless postmortem

videos.script: Every system fails. What a team controls is how long it hurts, and whether it happens the same way twice. {{fails}} Most incidents are not slow to fix. They are slow to declare. Forty minutes of people investigating in private, each thinking someone else is telling the customers. {{declare}} This lesson gives the hour a shape. One person decides. One person changes the system. One person talks to customers, on a clock, even when there is nothing new. {{roles}} It builds the timeline from what the systems recorded, not from memory. The deploy, the first error, the alarm, in order. {{timeline}} And it writes the review without blame, because a review that finds a person to blame stops looking at the system that let them fail. {{blameless}} By the end, you know what to do in the first five minutes, and what to write down after the last. {{end}}
